home.meta.title: Lin Wang — AI for Molecular Discovery
home.meta.description: Lin Wang develops computational methods for chemically informed molecular representation, structural modeling, and drug discovery.
home.hero.title:
Walking through
chemical space.
home.hero.statement: I develop computational methods that integrate chemical priors into molecular representation learning and generative drug design. My research spans AI-driven drug discovery and protein–ligand and protein–protein interaction modeling, with emerging directions in phenotype-based and polypharmacology drug design. My latest work, Ouroboros, advances this broader program through a molecular foundation model that learns chemically informed representations from conformational-space and pharmacophore similarities for molecular property prediction and generation.

home.scale.title: Ouroboros combines a shared molecular encoding with task-specific prediction and SMILES-decoding modules.
home.scale.encodeText: A GNN encodes molecular graphs as 2048-dimensional vectors; training uses fingerprint, conformational-space, and pharmacophore similarity matrices.
home.scale.navigateText: Task-specific property decoders score molecular encodings and define objectives used during latent-space search.
home.scale.decodeText: An autoregressive Transformer reconstructs candidate SMILES from input or modified encodings; the candidates require downstream evaluation.
home.dossier.deck: Ouroboros investigates whether chemically informed molecular representations can be reused for both prediction and generation. Its similarity-matrix objective integrates molecular fingerprints, conformational space, and pharmacophore relationships. Separate property decoders and an autoregressive SMILES decoder are used for the tasks evaluated in the study.
home.dossier.encodeText: A global-attention GNN maps each molecular graph to a 2048-dimensional vector. Training against molecular similarity matrices integrates fingerprint, conformational-space, and pharmacophore relationships.
home.dossier.navigateText: Relevant property decoders translate encodings into task-specific predictions and provide objectives for navigating the representation space.
home.dossier.decodeText: An autoregressive Transformer reconstructs SMILES from input or revised encodings, yielding candidate structures for subsequent prioritization and evaluation.
home.lineage.title: From pairwise similarity to similarity matrices.
home.lineage.intro: GeminiMol and Ouroboros both incorporate conformational-space and pharmacophore similarity. GeminiMol learns pairwise relationships, whereas Ouroboros extends supervision to full similarity matrices within each batch.
home.lineage.geminiText: GeminiMol learns from paired molecules, bringing encodings closer when their conformational and pharmacophore profiles are similar.
home.lineage.geminiValidation: Evaluated in similarity search and ligand-based virtual screening.
home.lineage.ouroborosText: Ouroboros supervises batches with full molecular similarity matrices, allowing multiple relative relationships to organize the encoding space together.
home.lineage.ouroborosValidation: Evaluated in property prediction, guided generation, and molecular-discovery case studies.

home.engine.title: A specified molecular objective can guide search in the learned encoding space.
home.engine.intro: The workflow begins with a measurable objective, such as a predicted property or similarity to a reference molecule. A selected decoder or similarity function scores encodings during search. The SMILES decoder then converts revised encodings into candidate structures that require further computational filtering and experimental assessment.
home.engine.flowAria: From a molecular design objective to candidate SMILES
home.engine.hypothesisText: A desired profile, reference molecule, phenotype, or target combination defines the search context.
home.engine.objectiveText: A property decoder or similarity function supplies the score used during search.
home.engine.navigationText: Search or iterative updates move molecular vectors toward a selected computational objective.
home.engine.reconstructionText: The decoder returns candidate SMILES for downstream computational and experimental assessment.
home.engine.applicationAlt: Ouroboros workflow connecting molecular design objectives with hit discovery and hit-to-lead optimization in representation space.
home.engine.applicationCaption: Evaluated search settings: exploration of chemical space and iterative optimization from a known hit. Open the full-resolution figure ↗
home.operations.intro: Within the study's formulation, a selected objective can be used in several complementary search settings.
home.operations.explorationText: For virtual screening or exploratory generation, predicted scores rank or guide candidates sampled from chemical space.
home.operations.migrationText: Starting from a known hit, the method iteratively updates its encoding while tracking similarity to the starting structure and selected predicted properties.
home.operations.fusionText: Several reference sets or objectives can be combined to propose candidates for a multi-target hypothesis; these remain computational proposals pending validation.
home.projects.title: Selected methods and collaborative studies.
home.projects.intro: This selection includes methods I led or co-developed and broader collaborative studies to which I contributed. Together they span molecular representation, phenotypic screening, protein structure and interactions, and synthetic accessibility.
home.projects.ouroboros.tagline: Property-guided molecular generation in a learned encoding space.
home.projects.ouroboros.detail: A molecular representation and generation framework combining similarity-matrix training, property decoders, and SMILES reconstruction.
home.projects.geminimol.tagline: Conformational-space profiling for general molecular representation.
home.projects.geminimol.detail: A representation-learning method incorporating conformational-space and pharmacophore similarity across molecular scaffolds.
home.projects.phenomodel.tagline: Aligning molecular graphs with cellular morphology.
home.projects.phenomodel.detail: A collaborative study of a multimodal model aligning molecular graphs with cell images for phenotypic virtual screening.
home.projects.proteinconformers.detail: A collaborative benchmark for assessing the diversity and plausibility of simulated protein conformational landscapes.
home.projects.ppiminer.tagline: Combining structural and sequence motifs for protein-interaction analysis.
home.projects.ppiminer.detail: A structure- and sequence-motif method for mining and modeling protein-protein interactions, evaluated in a CRBN substrate case study.
home.projects.deepsa.tagline: Predicting synthetic accessibility for molecular design.
home.projects.deepsa.detail: A co-developed deep-learning predictor of whether small molecules may be difficult to synthesize.
home.community.title: Open tools for everyday research.
home.community.intro: I also maintain or contribute to practical tools for database searching, molecular simulation, and reproducible computer-aided drug-design workflows.
home.community.biodb.description: A browser-based navigator that sends one query to multiple biomedical databases, designed to make routine literature and data lookup more direct.
home.community.automd.description: Automation for Desmond system setup and molecular-dynamics simulation, paired with a configurable pipeline for trajectory processing and analysis.
home.community.cadd.description: Shell utilities for virtual screening, cross-docking, and protein modeling with Schrödinger and Rosetta, shared to support reproducible computational workflows.

home.news.title: News
home.news.intro: Selected milestones from collaborative research, software releases, competitions, and publications, including the archive from the earlier site.
home.news.2026_ouroboros: The Ouroboros study, Learned Conformational Space and Pharmacophore Into Molecular Foundational Model, was published in Advanced Science.
home.news.2025_phenomodel: The PhenoModel study on multimodal phenotypic drug design was published in Acta Pharmaceutica Sinica B.
home.news.2024_11: The PhenoScreen project introduced a dual-space contrastive learning framework combining conformational-space and molecular-image similarities for virtual screening.
home.news.2024_09: A collaborative study using GeminiMol reported a GluN1/GluN3A inhibitor (IC50 = 0.98 μM); the project received first prize in the 2023 Shanghai International Computational Biology Innovation Competition.
home.news.2024_08: The GeminiMol paper was published in Advanced Science.
home.news.2023_12: The GeminiMol project introduced molecular representation learning informed by conformational-space similarity; see the code and bioRxiv preprint.
home.news.2023_10: DeepSA was published in the Journal of Cheminformatics; the DeepSA web server is also available.
home.news.2023_01: DeepSA, co-developed with Shihang Wang, was released as a model for estimating the synthetic accessibility of small molecules.
home.news.2022_12: The original plmd scripts were expanded and renamed AutoMD, adding support for additional force fields and configurable trajectory-analysis pipelines.
home.news.2022_11: The PPI-Miner study introduced a motif-driven method for protein-protein interaction mining and modeling. The paper appeared in the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling, with source code on GitHub.
home.news.2022_08: A computational library of potential CRBN substrates was released. Its entries are predicted candidates selected using β-hairpin and surface-complementarity criteria, not experimentally confirmed substrates.
home.news.2021_08a: A collaborative study reported an allosteric pocket on the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and inhibitor candidates designed to restrict its conformational change; the paper appeared in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry.
home.news.2021_08b: A collaborative study reported five candidate small-molecule blockers targeting the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in Acta Pharmacologica Sinica.
home.news.2021_05: Automated Schrödinger workflows for cross-docking (XDock), virtual screening (GVSrun), and molecular-dynamics simulation (plmd) were released, with source code on GitHub.
home.news.2020_05: Biodb-Search was released as a browser-based navigator that submits one query to multiple biomedical databases.
home.news.2019_12: GetPDB was released as a script for downloading single-chain protein structures by UniProt ID.
home.trajectory.title: Training and current research.
home.trajectory.intro: My training has progressed from life science and structure-based modeling to machine learning for molecules, proteins, and cellular phenotypes.
home.trajectory.bsText: Training in life science, followed by early work with computational drug-discovery workflows.
home.trajectory.phdText: Research in structural biology, molecular dynamics, protein interactions, and chemically informed molecular representation.
home.trajectory.postdocText: Research on molecular and protein machine-learning models, phenotype-aware representation learning, and computational drug-discovery applications.
home.contact.title: Research interests and collaboration.
home.contact.text: I welcome discussions and collaborations that connect molecular modeling and machine learning with experimentally testable drug-discovery questions.
